# Enigma 0.12.0
Queue messages while Enigma replies, copy code in one click, and sign in to ChatGPT or Claude in one step.
## New
- **Queue messages during a reply.** Keep typing while Enigma answers and press Return to queue up to five messages. They send in order. **Send now** sends one straight away, and **x** cancels it. - **Copy buttons.** Every code block has a **Copy** button; in terminal blocks it copies just the commands, without prompts or output. Finished replies have a **Copy reply** button that pastes cleanly into Mail or Pages. - **One-click ChatGPT and Claude sign-in.** Choosing **Sign in** now sets up what's missing for you: Enigma installs its own copy of Codex for ChatGPT, and runs Anthropic's installer for Claude Code. - **Screenshots with ChatGPT and Claude subscriptions.** When you're signed in to ChatGPT or Claude, **/screen** now works too. Their model lists refresh daily, so the newest ChatGPT models show up. - **Selected text in more apps.** Double-tap Option now picks up selections in Claude, Slack, Chrome, Safari (PDFs included) and other web-based apps. - **What's new?** After an update, a button at the top right of the window opens these notes.
## Improved
- **A fresh chat when you come back.** Enigma opens to a new chat at launch and after five minutes away. Saved chats stay in Recents, and a chat with a draft or a reply in progress is left alone. Empty chats are no longer saved. - **Selection chats continue in the window.** Once you send your question, the chat moves to the main window so you can carry on there. With **Keep selection chats private** off, they're saved to Recents. - **Texting the right person.** When several contacts share a name, Enigma asks which one you mean. With no earlier conversation, it texts a phone number, preferring mobile, rather than an email. - **Faster welcome setup.** Setup checks your Mac's performance once, not again for each model it installs. - **Clearer sign-in checks.** Check sign-in status now always shows its result under the row.
## Fixed
- The chat no longer scrolls into empty space after a long reply, and sending after scrolling up brings you back to the end. - The character no longer covers the model picker, other menus or the tour, or takes their clicks. - Enigma no longer says a message was sent when Messages failed to send it, and stops at once if macOS withholds a Messages permission. - Web searches no longer include slash commands, or personal details from screenshots and attached text. - Caps Lock no longer interrupts the double-Option shortcut. - Choosing more than 16 files or folders now says so and keeps your current attachments. - Fixed a crash when Codex or Claude Code quit while a large screenshot was being sent.

# Enigma 0.11.0
Bigger local models that stay fast, commands that understand plain wording, and downloads that survive a dropped connection.
- **Recommendations fit your Mac's real speed.** Enigma measures your Mac's memory bandwidth with a quick GPU test and recommends the smartest model that still replies quickly. On a 24 GB M5 Pro that is now Gemma 4 12B instead of Qwen3.5 4B. - **Commands from plain wording.** Turn on **Settings → General → Commands → Recognize commands from your wording** and Enigma turns on the matching command as you type, shown as a chip in the composer. "Has Dad replied yet" or "text Sam that I'm here" uses Messages; "take your time" or "double-check your answer" turns on thinking; "make this more formal" with selected text becomes an **/edit**; "translate this" translates. It runs on fixed rules on this Mac, with no extra model call, and is off until you turn it on. - **Bigger models on smaller Macs.** The larger families now come in 3-bit and IQ4_XS sizes too. On a 24 GB Mac, Qwen3.8 27B fits at 3 bits and is offered as **smarter, slower replies**. A model that is fast at some size uses its highest-precision fast size; one that is fast at none offers its smallest IQ4_XS-or-better size that still reaches 8 tokens per second, and drops to 3 bits only when none does. A 3-bit model counts as 15% less capable when the choices are ranked, so it wins only when it is clearly stronger, and when it is recommended, its own 4-bit size can be offered as **smarter, slower replies**. Speed estimates for the new IQ sizes may be optimistic until you run **Check performance**. - **A refreshed catalogue.** New: Qwen3.5 2B, Qwen3.6 35B-A3B, Qwen3.8 27B and Gemma 4 31B, plus more sizes of Qwen3.5 9B, Gemma 4 12B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B, for Macs from 8 GB to 128 GB. Gemma 4 E4B and Ministral 3 8B and 14B stay, mostly as choices under **All models**; copies installed with 0.10.1 show **Update** once, which downloads the same files again to move them to the new llama.cpp. SmolVLM2 and MiniCPM-o leave the catalogue; installed copies keep working under **On this Mac**. - **Three clear choices.** Every picker shows the same **recommended**, **faster** and **smarter, slower replies** options. - **Downloads survive a dropped connection.** A brief Wi-Fi drop no longer restarts a model download: each part resumes from the bytes already on disk. While a model downloads and installs, Enigma keeps the Mac from idle-sleeping; the display can still sleep. - **Keep chatting while a model downloads.** Cloud chat and your current local model work during a download; Enigma waits for the reply in progress before switching to the new model. - **Selected text in VS Code.** Double-tap Option now picks up text selected in VS Code and editors built on it (VS Code Insiders, VSCodium, Cursor, Windsurf). Enigma uses their copy only when VS Code confirms a real selection, so a whole line you didn't select is never attached, and your clipboard is put back afterwards. - **One Local models page.** Settings → Discover and Hugging Face file downloads are gone. Settings → Local models shows the choices for this Mac, your installed models and every catalogue model. - **Check this Mac** replaces **Detect Mac capabilities** and **Refresh recommendations**, and measures the bandwidth again. - **A newer llama.cpp (b11734)** reads full-screen screenshots on Gemma 4 correctly. Installed models show **Update** once, which downloads the package again; until then the installed copy keeps working. - **/screen no longer stalls on the first capture.** When macOS is slow to start reading text, Enigma stops waiting after three seconds and lets the model read the image instead. - **Smoother long replies.** Streaming replies parse their Markdown as they arrive instead of starting over with each new piece, so long answers stay responsive. - **Models no longer in the catalogue get no update.** They, including Gemma 4 12B QAT, stay on their old llama.cpp runtime, which misreads screenshots on Gemma models. If you use Gemma 4 12B QAT for screenshots, install the new Gemma 4 12B from Settings → Local models.

# Enigma 0.10.1
A tidier sidebar.
- **Developer Tools is gone from the sidebar.** It was meant for testing Enigma, not for everyday use. - **Its tools are in Settings.** **Detect Mac capabilities** is in Settings → Local models, which now also shows your Mac's CPU count and Metal support. **Replay welcome setup** stays in Settings → General.

# Enigma 0.10.0
Enigma now keeps itself up to date.
- **Updates arrive by themselves.** Once a day Enigma checks for a new version, downloads it, and installs it the next time it quits. This is the last version you need to download by hand. - **Restart when it suits you.** When an update is ready, the menu-bar menu shows **Restart to Update**. Choose it to install now, or keep working and it installs when Enigma quits. - **You stay in control.** Settings → General → Updates has two switches: one for the daily check and one for downloading and installing automatically. **Check Now** looks for an update straight away. - **It settles into Applications.** If you open Enigma from Downloads or anywhere else, it offers to move itself into Applications and reopen, because it can only update itself from there. - **Shortcuts that stay out of the way.** ⌥⌃ now opens Enigma only when you press and release those two keys on their own, so other apps' ⌃⌥ shortcuts no longer open it. Show or hide chat history with **⌃⌘S**, open the selection panel's chat in the window with **⌘O**, and attach files with **⇧⌘A**. The Option-S shortcut for Settings is gone, so Option-S types its character again; use **⌘,** or the menu-bar menu. - **Your permissions stay.** Updates keep Enigma's identity, so Screen Recording, Accessibility and your saved keys carry over.
Only Enigma's version number is sent when it checks for updates.
